title: Two Oceans in One Tank
logline: A transparent miniature Bering Sea lets the viewer watch an AI harvest rule learn, then reveals why changing the biology changes what a promising result means.
cold_open: 0 to 3 seconds: camera rushes underwater toward a silver pollock. The entire ocean abruptly slides backward inside a glass tank. The fish looks toward the passing seafloor. Clear corner label: SIMULATION. The impossible rewind establishes that seasons can be tried again.

escalation.picture: Pull out from macro fish scale to a tabletop-sized transparent test tank suspended over an illustrated Bering Sea map. Two separate output windows identify CATCH and BREEDING STOCK. Publication stamp names the September 11th paper. First promise: what counts as a better rule?

Extreme close cutaway into the tank's learning mechanism. A candidate harvest-rule tile enters a simulated season, two outcome labels return feedback, and the candidate changes before the next trial. Beside it a predefined-rule tile stays fixed. Mark the whole mechanism SCHEMATIC, with no numerical reward formula.

Low underwater view of a labeled CONSTANT RECRUITMENT inlet. Catch and breeding-stock comparison windows unfold separately: LARGE ANNUAL CATCH SWINGS and HIGHER BREEDING BIOMASS. The tank retains the same identifiable copper rim.

A second inlet assembly hovers above the first: STOCK-LINKED RECRUITMENT. Plant the second promise: does the breeding-stock advantage survive a different biological assumption? Pause before inserting it.

The inlet changes. The two outcome windows now read HIGHER CATCH and LOWER BREEDING BIOMASS, each explicitly VERSUS ITS COMPARISON. Pay the second loop at 70 seconds. No annual-stability claim and no quantitative fish-count bars.

ACT 3 TEST, THE TANK'S EDGE: zoom from the model to a full harbor panorama. A tiny simulated boat tries to cross the acrylic rim and stops. Inside, the two candidate outcomes remain real research findings; outside, neutral labels show untested real-world performance and stakeholder goals. The tank visibly doesn't contain the harbor.

Return to overhead test-tank view. Its two outcome windows stay open together. The advantage now is examining alternatives against named goals. Resolve the first loop at 103 seconds: there isn't a demonstrated winning real-world rule, but there are specific choices to test.

the_turn: The breeding-stock comparison reverses when recruitment changes. The visual pays this as a new experiment, then exposes the model boundary at full scale. More catch and more breeding biomass aren't interchangeable achievements.

button.last_line_intent: Ask what balance of catches, annual stability and breeding fish a candidate rule should have to demonstrate.
button.last_image: The opening pollock faces two open outcome windows inside the same copper-rimmed tank. Nothing receives a winner's crown. The fish flicks its tail, matching the opening motion.

sight_gags.gag: The simulated fish briefly swims forward while its ocean rewinds behind it, then turns to inspect the inconsistency.
The fixed comparison-rule tile remains perfectly still while the learned tile changes its outfit after feedback; mechanism rather than personality establishes the joke.
A miniature boat reaches the transparent tank wall. Its wake continues half a beat, then neatly folds back inside the model.

retention_plan.the_test: The Tank's Edge grants the strongest objection: internally informative outcomes don't demonstrate real-fishery usefulness, livelihoods or operational superiority. Draw the full harbor beyond the small model, then retain only the earned claim of policy exploration.

states: Changed recruitment and reversed biomass comparison at 58s
Bounded research tool beside real harbor at 74s
Two outcomes held together in final image

two_loops: Planted by15s: what makes a rule better? Paid103s with explicit multiple outcomes and no demonstrated operational winner.
Planted44s: does the breeding-stock advantage survive changed recruitment? Paid70s with the opposite biomass comparison.
retention_plan.padding_test: Removing the biological reversal would falsely generalize the first result. Removing the tank-edge test would overstate real-world value. Removing the return to both output windows would leave a generic caution instead of an actionable research question. Each advances rather than repeats the argument.

production_plan.guardrails: Schematic labels remain legible. No invented numerical curves, apparent measured fish counts, reward formula, quota-adoption claim, smoother-catch implication or office paperwork world.
